title: Requires more effort than it helps.
body:
AI planner is awful, often giving inaccurate timings (you tell it that you need to do a task before midday, and it schedules it for 12:15) and needing amending, but only lets you accept or reject all of the actions it presents, rather than selecting which ones it got right or wrong. 

Manually inputting reminders is tedious and there is no separation between early and late afternoon. 

It also really pushes you to upgrade to premium (as soon as you open the app, what feels like every single time) which can interrupt your train of thought or when you want to note something down before you forget. 

The homescreen widgets add little to no useful functionality, and have a massive “upgrade to premium” badge. 

For an app designed to help you plan and declutter your brain, it sure does require a lot of micromanagement. 

To be honest the default iOS calendar and reminder apps are far more intuitive and do everything you’d need.

title: Not a scam!
body: Coming from someone with ADHD this app isn’t actually BS, which I was pleasantly surprised by. For some background, I am a student that was diagnosed 3-4 years ago and have been on meds for 2-3. I hyperfocus on all the wrong things and don’t get any actual tasks done. With poor executive dysfunction and even poorer time management, I struggle to stick to timetabled tasks and half the time I don’t even know what tasks I’m supposed to be doing. This app tackles that really well: the to-do function lets your create a detailed and well-organised list personal to you, that you can further improve by labelling tasks as high, medium and low priority, and this really helps put work into perspective. Additionally, the different features of the app such as the routines allow for breakdown of tasks, which is also really helpful for someone who struggles with tasks that ‘feel big.’ The only feedback I would give is that I wish there were more free features - already there are tons, which I appreciate greatly (so don’t change that), and if I had the money I think it would be worth it as everything I have experienced on the app so far has been very useful for my daily life. Unfortunately I don’t, so I am just using review this to beg for more given that the app is already incredibly useful for free. Otherwise, I highly recommend Tiimo!

title: Used to be fantastic, now it’s disappointing.
body:
I’ve used this app for nearly 4 years now. I really liked the routines feature, my school had a really odd timetable format and Tiimo could accommodate that. When they got rid of the routines feature earlier this year, I was bummed. It was almost the only thing that set this app apart from the others and I know it is missed by many users. I’ve left school since and just kind of put up with it (so now all of my days have many, many tasks which used to be condensed into one routine), but one thing that irks me now that didn’t happen before is the fact that I can’t have a task start or end in anything that isn’t a 0 or a 5. I can understand why, as that’s most anybody would need, but for example I take a train at 7:23 every morning and have had to compromise on being precise.

I am also really not a fan of the whole AI thing. I don’t like being randomly notified throughout the day about check-ins and supposedly motivational messages, I don’t mean to sound like a right grumpy person but I personally just find it annoying. I’d rather just be notified about my tasks, and nothing else.

I have given it 2 stars and not 1 because the Apple Watch app is a good feature. It breaks… a lot… but overall it is a feature that I don’t see elsewhere.

I don’t think it’s an outright scam as some other reviews claim, but after using it for 4 years I think I might start looking for other options. I miss the old Tiimo, the Tiimo with routines and just a basic but streamlined experience with no unnecessary frills.

author: Xenopus15

title: Routines
body:
I used this app for years and loved it so much. I realised I stopped using it for a year when the routine function was taken away. The ability to have a whole routine that can be added on to your calendar was so good. You could set each sub task in the routine to have its own time frame and the visual timer would show how long you had left of that task before the next one would start, it was brilliant. Additionally I love how when you start a task you don’t need to stay on the app to see the timer, it will automatically show on your Lock Screen forcing me to stay aware of my timings and tasks, preventing me from procrastination or getting distracted because the timer is right in front of your face each time you look at your phone. 
However I realised I stopped using the app when routines was taken away. I found it meticulous to have to add each task in separately in order to reek the benefits of the visual timer and holding myself accountable for completing sub tasks within the time frame. Now the visual timer just has the timing for the whole routine and the sub tasks in the routine is now a check list. I didn’t realise how much this impacted my time keeping skills till it was gone! 

For example my morning routine used to have time frames for each morning task, 10 minutes for breakfast, 2 minutes for brushing my teeth etc and I could see the timing of the sub tasks on the visual timer on my Lock Screen making sure I don’t go over or it will change to the next sub task. Now the visual timer just shows 1 hour morning routine with my sub tasks as a check list which doesn’t help me stay within my time limit.

This app is so good but I have had to unsubscribe from the subscription due to routines been taken away and I have simply stopped using the app due to this. PLEASE BRING THEM BACK!

title: One App To Rule Them All
body:
Tiimo is an absolute game-changer for time management, planning, and productivity—especially for those with ADHD and other neurodivergent minds! The app’s visual, intuitive design makes it easy to structure my day without feeling overwhelmed. Features like gentle reminders, color coding, and a distraction-free interface help me stay on track without the stress of rigid schedules.

What truly makes Tiimo stand out is its understanding of neurodiversity. It’s designed with flexibility in mind, making it a fantastic tool for those who struggle with executive functioning. Plus, the customer support is phenomenal—responsive, kind, and always helpful.

If you’re looking for a planner that actually works with your brain, rather than against it, I highly recommend Tiimo!

title: Updated: finally a digital brain that takes the pressure off!
body:
Updated review
Having previously been really disappointed what can I say but, wow! What an improvement !

A friend begged me to give it another grow and all my previous concerns have been dealt with. 

Once you follow the advice to watch the video when getting started, it’s pretty much smooth sailing and your original investment in set up really pus off. 

It’s so easy to move tasks to a later date, even if they’re recurring meaning you don’t have to worry about them getting lost or forgotten. Oh, and the flexibility when scheduling tasks is really helpful - want it on every second Tuesday at 3pm? No problem!

The checklists are great for breaking down tasks so, firstly, you don’t get overwhelmed and secondly, you can complete some of the steps and reschedule the remainder. It really takes the pressure and sense of failure off. 

The AI aspects are mostly helpful with the great majority of suggestions being helpful. 

Also, the fact that tasks don’t disappear even if you completed them a while ago is really helpful. 

Tiimo really does act as a digital brain now and cuts down the amount of apps you need to use. 

Now, using the app is a great experience so well done to the team. 

Original review
Tiimo has the potential to be a great app but fails on the execution. Let’s start with the good. The ability to time block your day in the same app as your calendar appears is great. Routines so you don’t have to add each activity individually definitely saves times and being able to set up recurring activities adds to this. Being able to add checklists to your activities is useful for staying on task as well as remembering what you intended when you come back to an activity. Being able to add a note to an activity is also helpful in keeping things in one place and allowing you to ‘brain dump’ with confidence. Other productivity hacks like automated reminders are also present and add to its usefulness. However… If you accidentally add an activity to a routine that isn’t already in your activities, you’ll have to go there to add it again. You also end up with activities that you’ve added as a one off to your day appearing in your activity store meaning you quickly end up with an unwieldy list. Updated routines aren’t reflected in the calendar - you need to delete the routine and then add it again. Also if you update a routine you then have the original and the updated one in your store. Notes are *not* synced. You therefore lose all your unallocated tasks if you have to delete the app because of bugs, as happened to me. That means using yet another app to keep your notes. This is perhaps the dealbreaker. I use the app to try to keep everything in one place and reduce the number of apps I use to stay productive. To lose all those planned tasks is devastating for productivity and confidence in the app and destroys the point of subscribing in that you need a back up for unallocated activities. Overall it’s an app I might use if it was free but wouldn’t subscribe to again. It requires a lot of investment to learn how to use and given that, and losing all your tasks when you encounter an app bug meaning you have to use yet another app for that just means it’s not worth the money. Maybe in the future when there are fewer bugs and notes sync I might reconsider but for now it’s back to looking for the holy grail of productivity apps. 😔

title: It works
body:
I have tried so many of these apps to try and organise my neurodivergent self. They are mostly annoying. 

This one is fantastic. The AI task generator is brilliant, you can tweak it a little if you want to make it more personal to your activity, but it’s very good at picking accurate tasks for a chosen activity. I’ve got it so far to generate tasks for cleaning the kitchen, applying for a job, tidying the bedroom, collecting my shopping, colouring my hair, going to the cinema, and getting ready for work on Monday. It does it so well, and you can tick the tasks off as you do them. It’s so useful to look and see what you’re supposed to do next, it stops you getting distracted and doing something else.

You get reminders, you get time updates while you’re doing an activity, you can check off everything. You can add “pick up shopping” or similar and you get timely reminders. If you need a break, you can pause the activity. If you’re unable to do the activity at the time you planned, you can reschedule it. If you’re doing an activity and the time runs out, you can add five minutes. Apple Watch users can do this on their watch as well, which is fab. 

You can integrate your calendar, selecting only the ones you want reminded of. I need to find out how to stop them being “activities” though, I don’t need reminded all day that a birthday has 15 hours to go. Lol. 

This app does what it claims and I couldn’t be happier. I see that they have fixed the glitches that other users mentioned. Good app for those of us who are disorganised and forgetful. I am halfway through the trial and will be signing up for the very, very reasonable £22.49 for a year. That’s brilliant.

title: Inflexible, hard to use and patronising
body: Tried the app as something for prompts and planning on days when executive function is a challenge. Looked promising at first but it is a stressful experience trying to setup your own tasks and routines, as you need to know exactly when everything is, how long it lasts and checklists at each point. And there is no web app so this all has to be done on a little phone keyboard. There is no option to have an inbox or staging area to braindump activities for later or bump things back into if time slots become full with higher priority work. Once a task starts good luck staying on task; parts of routines fly by automatically even if you are still on them, you can’t control the timer and it just becomes panic-inducing as you have no control over the system if you have to take a phone call or anything. Completed activities have a patronising little bit of confetti and painfully slow animation adding friction as well. To top it off while there are some semi-useful templates, the input system is so clunky it is just as much hassle as starting from scratch, and there are contributions from some rather aggressive social media prevented who are very, very big on hammering home just how much better their (overly influencer) ways are *the* only way to do things and how can you call yourself autistic if you dare to not be like them? It just makes the whole thing seem like a clique and rather toxic. It is a nice idea on paper, but despite trying time and again Tiimo just makes me more stressed and burned out with tasks than actually fixing anything.

title: An absolute lifesaver for those with learning differences
body:
I don’t normally leave app reviews but if there’s one app that deserves it it’s Tiimo. Developing a routine and positive habits is a continuous challenge for me, and my as-yet-untreated ADHD has caused me to try almost every app on the App Store to organise myself. I somehow keep returning to Tiimo however, a year after I first signed up.

Firstly, Tiimo has an incredibly user friendly interface, and it feels pleasant to use. There are lots of different icons available to visually distinguish between activities and tasks. On the premium membership, importing your calendar events is seamless.

Several features really make Tiimo stand apart from other planning tools. Unlike just using Apple Calendar, for example, Tiimo has a timer view that allows you to only see what you’re working on right now. For someone like me that is prone to distraction this is critical. No other apps seem to implement this in the same way as Tiimo.

Another feature is that there are several different ‘levels’ available for your activities and tasks. For example, you could have a single activity as it’s own timer, or if you’re working on something that has lots of steps you can use checklists that sit below a particular activity. Activities themselves can be combined as part of routines that themselves can be saved, set to repeat and so on. 

I’ve found the most effective mornings I’ve had over the past year have been ones where I have all my morning activities laid out for me in advance and I can just move my way through the timers. Otherwise I never get anywhere!

As a final point, the app is specifically designed for folks with specific challenges, be this ASD, ADHD, and so on, and as such I find it fits my brain really well. Knowing that this user base is in mind in every step of the design process is fantastic, and I believe the team deserve all the credit for their hard work. They’re also incredibly open to suggestions and feedback, and the subscription price I feel is incredibly reasonable for an app that you can use every single day, all day long, for all manner of uses. It particularly shines when used in conjunction with a smart watch (e.g. the Apple Watch) as I can leave my phone somewhere else as I just follow the timers on my wrist.

I could keep going so I’ll stop here! Thank you for developing Tiimo - the community feels so supportive and positive and it’s brought a little bit of light into my life while I’ve been navigating receiving an ADHD diagnosis as an adult.

title: Oh no. Oh no. Oh no no no no
body:
I used to absolutely adore this app. It changed my life. So much so that a couple of months ago I decided I’m going to take the plunge and lay for the yearly subscription.

Oh dear. The new update means routines are now set up by duration rather than specific time. Apparently everyone wanted this. I do not.

As an autistic human I am stereotyping myself here but change is not my friend. I am autistic with Conor I’d ADD and dyscalculia so numbers are not friend either.

I used to set up Tiimo every Sunday and create a new routine based on what I had in the new week. I also used to delete the old one first because I can’t stand clutter (BIG mistake that turned out to be!)

Now, instead of saying drink 5 sips of water every hour (I despise water, hate it, but I know I should drink it and having the app tell me every hour to take just 5 sips gets me through 2.5 litres a day, well, it used to) NOW I have to dedicate 18 hours on my day off to try and guess (as we know, time doesn’t look the same to neuroatypicals) how many minutes it’ll take me to brush my teeth use the bathroom and shower then set drink water for an hour which is obviously not right and also add everything else at the same time as drink water for an at best guessed amount of minutes which means 14 notifications an hour which … well .. I can’t dedicate that amount of time to setting up individual activities for set times for every day that’ll drive me insane.

Heartbroken that I deleted my old base routine, at least I would’ve had a starting point but with the update I would’ve just been told to drink water every 2 minutes … and heartbroken that something that worked SO well is no obsolete to me. Heartbroken that I have another 9 months on a subscription I won’t use anymore. And heartbroken that I now I have to go through the hideous task of looking for a new planner app, getting used to a new planner app, probably several until I find meh it’ll do.  

Guess it’s back to setting 498 alarms on my phone. Or better yet, just buy actual alarm clocks and set them and stick post it’s on them to tell me what to do at a specific time because at least no one can update an alarm clock overnight and decrease the quality of my life significantly in one fell swoop. I guess the majority have spoken. Bye Tiimo the last year had been fun now you’re just someone that I used to appreciate

title: Life-changing app
body: Been looking for a routine design app for such a long time, have tried them all out and this one is the one I keep coming back to. Initially had the two week trial and loved it but was reluctant to pay for a subscription. Stopped using for a while but I found my life crumbled back into chaos without it which proved to me it’s worth every penny. It takes away all the decision making for you in your daily life, it’s like having a second brain nudging you to do all your tasks. Absolutely perfect if you have ADHD. I use a combination of this app, Todoist and google calendar and it’s working pretty well! The setup, however, is rather fiddly and I have found myself frustrated with how long it takes to set up the routines. I sent a message to the team asking if this was going to be improved and they got back to me within minutes with an estimated timeline for updates. Feels really nice to support a small team of developers and to know they’re listening to users. Makes you feel like you’re part of it, creating a real tool that can make a big difference to people’s lives. Never felt like that with an app before! Perhaps I’m over dramatising, but after such a long search for something that can genuinely help me, it feels pretty special to find something that works.

title: Life saver
body: I rarely leave reviews.  But this deserves it.  1) web user interface is best place to set schedules I find. Small learning curve. Set a days schedule first, then create a routine. But after that in my daily life this is great place to start. I have many work projects on the go by necessity. Sometimes I would stall because I didn’t know what to do next. I got exhausted. But this app allows me to clearly break down my day into regular routines so things get done. No distractions. Connects with my dirt cheap smart watch (amazon deal at £25). Reminds me on a root setting 5 mins before a task switch. And half way through a task in case I’ve gotten distracted. The calendar on web is a delight to work with. Clearly shows if there is a clash. Only thing I’d change on the web is perhaps a bit clearer where there are time gaps between schedules things. Ideally I’d love to zoom into a calendar and it increase the resolution of time. (Zoom out and it’s listed by hours, zoom in and you get 30 mins. Zoom further 15 mins. Zoom again 10 mins). Then just drag things around rather than going in and changing times. That said, it really is wonderful. Far more visual and clear than other calendars. Individual tasks set in activities is excellent now. And being able to edit my routine items individually without nag screens about changing all acticitivities. Only thing I haven’t discovered yet is once a routine is set up, being able to go into the routine activity at the top level and edit the routine there. But that may make it too complicated. Well worth it. Oh... and the support is fantastic too.

title: Great idea but overall frustrating
body:
The premise of this app is amazing but so far I am finding it very hard to use. It would be helpful to be able to add a length to an activity rather than an end time, as well as the ability to swap activities around by dragging and dropping. Currently it takes an excessive amount of time to change the times for each day when I have alternating schedules, or I want to start an activity now rather than its usual time. This is particularly important to me since the days and shifts I work vary week by week. I am hoping the ability to just create a new activity with a length rather than time is included in the new flexible activities feature. 

Creating new routines is also hard to work out. It is stressful since you cannot create new activities from the routine menu and there are no explanations or tips for this. It would also be helpful to be able to preview the content of the tiimo routines before adding to your day, since otherwise I cannot judge if it will be helpful for me. 

Perhaps the reason I am disappointed with the app functionality is because I heard of it through YouTube videos that promised more flexibility and the ability to create routines rather than schedules. Lastly, I do not receive notifications at all despite having switched on all the settings. 

Hopefully I will be able to use this soon once fixes for these issues have been published, however for now I will have to unsubscribe as the app is not properly functional at this stage.

title: Not customisable at all!
body:
The routines are not as customisable as they claim and when I offered feedback about this, the developers didn't even read the feedback I offered, instead providing a 'form' response because they skim-read what I wrote and thought I was saying that it isn't customisable at all.

I wish I could give 0 stars.

1) You can delete the built-in routines that you don't want, BUT THEY COME BACK AGAIN AFTERWARDS!!! What is the point in deleting them in that case???
2) You can't delete the built-in activities, nor can you edit the icon or the times.
3) When you edit an activity's start time, the  end time doesn't change to match (so if you've set up a 2hr activity, and move it to be an hour earlier, it becomes a 3hr activity)
4) You can't set a repeating activity up, but then delete just one of them, eg I only workout on the days I'm not going to work - I can't have a repeating "Workout" activity and remove them from my working days; I have to add the Workout manually 5 times a week - very time consuming. 

In short… I installed this app in the hope that it would make sure I do the things I need to do, and reduce my meltdowns, but the UX is *such* a nightmare that I had multiple meltdowns just trying to set my schedule up!! Goodbye, useless app.
